data.name: Dulciana
data.long_meaning: The name Dulciana is derived from the Latin word 'dulcis', meaning 'sweet' or 'pleasant'. This name was often used in medieval literature as a term of endearment and was also given to girls born during the Christmas season. In Christian tradition, the name is reminiscent of the sweetness and gentleness of the infant Jesus.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the sweet and gentle nature of the Virgin Mary and the love and compassion of God.
data.numerology_meaning: A name that signifies new beginnings and leadership.

historical_references.reference: The legend of Saint Dulciana of Albi dates back to the 11th century. According to the story, she was a beautiful and pious young girl who was courted by the count of Albi, but she rejected his advances and remained devoted to God. In return, she was persecuted and imprisoned. Through prayers and divine intervention, she was miraculously freed, converted the count, and founded a monastery in Albi. This story was popularized through the writings of the 13th-century French historian, Geoffrey of Vigeois.

Another reference to Saint Dulciana comes from the 15th-century 'Golden Legend' by Jacobus de Voragine. In this compilation of hagiographies, Dulciana is described as a noblewoman of Albi who was falsely accused of adultery and condemned to be burned alive. However, she was saved by a miracle and converted her accusers. She lived as a hermit for the rest of her life, and her relics were venerated in Albi until the French Revolution.
